cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Avaranga in Kōviartana-vishaya as a dhiga to the god Jaṁmavardeva in the village. The date of coronation of the King is given as Śaka 980.

From a set of impressions received in the office from the Jubraj of Tekkali. Registers the grant of some land in the village Haribhata, situated in the Kroshpākavartani, free of taxes, as devāgrāha for worship and offerings and repairs in the temple of Hamēśvara-Bhaṭṭāraka. The king bears the title Rajasiṁha. The inscription mentions the pradhānāchārya (minister) of Bhānu-chandra and was engraved by Stagnōnju.

Hesus to register a gift of land to the temple of Mūlashāna Kālīdeva at Vuņḍavare (f) by Bommeya-Nāyaka, a minister of the king who calls himself a great devotee of Bhūtanātha-dēva. Refers to the siege of the fortress Toraṅgallu during a great battle in which the king was victorious.

cells.date: Śaka 1173, Piavaṅga (wrong), Jyeshṭha, paurnima, Thureday, lunar eolipse.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of shares in the village Niherura to a number of brahmans by Malli-Śreshthi, the son-in-law of Bhōtirāya, the governor under the Yadava king.

cells.date: Śaka 1272, Bahudhānya, Māgha, ba. amāvāsyā, Sunday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: The king bears a number of birudas. Gift of the village Nāgireddipalle, as carva-mānya, to the brahmon 11ēvatasa, son of Bhaskaradēva, by the king.

Plates missing in the beginning. Registers the grant of Tinnamasamudram in Kangsani-palli a village in the Gutti sub-division, to Appalachārya, son of Tiruvēṅkaṭa Tāṭāchārya and grandson of Penugonda Appayā-chārya. The grant was engraved by śaṅkhaṭāchārya. The sign-manual of the king is engraved in Telugu as 'Śrī-Pirupāksha'.
Records the grant of the village of Rudra-varti. The letters are badly engraved The sign-manual 'Śrī-Virupāksha' is en-graved in Kannaḍa.

Registers the grant of Raghavanmapēta, the hamlet of Mushtūru, as a svayānto to Krish-ṇamāchārya, son of Tiruvēṅkaṭāchārya and the grandson of Pēraṅguri Venkaṭāchārya of the Gārgya-sōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra.
Records the confirmation by several indivi-duals of the ollae of the Reddi of Badalli village, on a certain Morasa Nāgi-Redḍi, as a hereditary privileges.

Records the gift of the right of parashthiya in their community to a certain Kesavārya, son of Purushōttamayya and the grandson of L'augonda Narabarappa, of the Kaundinya-sāgōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra, by a number of Arya-Kshatriyas of the Muktarishi-vamsa, whose names were given. It also settles the fees that this priest was entitled to receive in their families on the several occasions.

cells.date: Śaka 1439, Nandana (wrong), Vaisakha, paurpima, Visakba, Bhpigu.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the parashthiyam right in their families to a certain Narasimga, son of Appaya and grandson of Purushōttama of the Kaundinya-gōtra and Yajur-vēda by roverl members of the Malla community, whose namet are given.

Purports to register the grant of the tenure called desapēkarānikam to a certain Tiru-mula-mallur, by Mohanupalasya Bhu-jabala Sommadvardya-Mahādivya, an agent of the king, and gives a list of fields granted to him as remuneration in several villages.
South-Indian Inscriptions.

Purports to register the conferment of the ređdirikam right over Dharmavaram, in equal shares, on two families during the regime of Samprati Tipparajayya over Pennamagaṇi in Gutti-rajya. Also specifies several individuals as the holders of the various offices in the village, and the extent of the lands allotted to them. Mentions a Chikka-Ođeya as having constructed the Dharmavaram tank and as having brought the idol of Chennakeśavasvami from Anegondi and consecrated it in the village.

The copper-plate bears on its top a solid image of two figures riding one behind the other on a single horse, the group being overshadowed by a serpent-hood. Purports to register the conferment of the gōtī-gadda right over the village Nasana in the Kanaganapalli-sīma, a sub-division of Palēgāṁala in Guṭṭi-rājya, to Peda Chodamē-Reddi, and enumerates the lands granted to him.

cells.date: Śaka 1467, Viśvavasu, Karttika, Saturday, sn. Utthana-dvadaśi.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Tumicherla otherwise called Ramachandrapuram, as sareamānya to a number of brahmans at the request of Tōtapa-Nayaka, who was a subordinate of the king and was the son of Konđama-Nayaka and grandson of Tōtapa. The village was divided into 4C shares.

cells.date: Śaka 1665, Telugu Rudhirodgāri, Bhadrapada, śu. 10, Wednesday.
cells.remarks: Records the grant as vṛittiyam of a village called Veṅkaṭāpuram formed out of the two hamlets of Tirumalapēpa and Bhatāpuram in the Marangi-ṭālūku, which were part of the estate of the donor Rajah Sri Satrucherla Gangarajugaru to Tirumala Veṅkaṭa-rangachāryulu-Ayyavarlu, with the stipulation that the donee should pay Rs. 100 a year (as rent).

Purports to record the permission which the king granted, on the occasion of his visit to Bavaḷippaṭṭu, (when he was pleased with the reception accorded to him by the chief and four families from the north), to a certain Oṇḍipuḷi-Nāyaka, to found a village in the latter's name and serve as a pāḷaiyakkāran after paying a tax to him. The surplus of revenue after deducting 370 poṇ for himself as the pāḷaiyakkāran and 70 poṇ as nāḍumāṉi-māṉiyam, was directed to be sent to the kachcheri at Madurāpuri.

Read for this office by Mr. G. Ramadas of Jeypore. Records a gift of 10 garce of land, and a grant by the king to the Juṅgan Pramabhu-pūjāri, of the priests of the two temples of Mallikārjuna, for offerings to the deities during the three courses of worship of the day.
A single brass-plate document in obscure characters resembling Kannaḍa. The first line is more easily traceable as Kannaḍa.

Registers the remission of certain customary taxes and the levy of an amount of Ks. 16 a year in the śrōtriya village of Venkata-krishnarayapuram.

cells.king: Kulasekhara-Sambuvarāya †
cells.remarks: Records the order of Kulasekhara-Sambuvarāya granting, from the 10th year of the king's reign] certain taxes due on the temple lands to a certain Nāganāni-Dēvapparumal, with the stipulation that he and his descendants should provide for the daily offerings during the service Sevyal-venyōnad in the temple of Pallikonda-Perumāl st. Vichchur, and feed five itinerant brahman pilgrims in the temple with the offered rice.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the same transaction and addresses the order to Nāganāni-Dēvapparumal mentioned above.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the order of the same chief addressed to the residents of Kilai-Vichchur remitting the taxes on the portions of lands other than those belonging to the temple for the maintenance of offerings in the service referred to above.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records an order of the same chief to the residents of Vēppur granting two vēli of land as tiruniramātam, exempt from all taxes, to the temple from the 10+ 1st year (of the king's reign).

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the order of the same chief to the residents of Tagadarnāḍu|valanāḍu remitting certain

cells.place: On the base of the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: An order by the same chief to the tāgattār of the temple of Pallikonda-Perumāl at Kīlai-Vichchūr, conferring on Nayimiśai-Dēvapporumāl (mentioned above) the right of worship in the temple for five days, and the grant of a free house.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1058, Ānanda, Pushya, amāvāsyā, Sunday, solar eclipse. The details are irregular, but the date intended was probably A.D. 1135, January 16, Wednesday, solar eclipse, if we consider that the week-day 'Sunday' given in the record as a mistake. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 461]
cells.remarks: Records a sarvamānya gift by the same chief (Kulaśekhara Sambuvarayan) of the villages Tagadūrnadāl, vanpatṭtu and [Ni]prettam s tiruvidaipāttam for the provision of offerings in the temple of Pallikonḍa-Perumā.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Records an order of the chief Sambuvarāyan as to the remissions of Tagadarnāḍuvalanāḍu remitting as sreeramānya the several taxes due from them other than those on the dēvadāna lands, in favour of the temple for worship, offerings, and repairs. Sesirayar and Kadu-ve[ttigai] figure as signatories.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to record a similar order of the king to the residents of Ulogakachobi alias Araśaril-aṇjada-peruma|nallar through Kulaśekhara-Sambuvarāyan, granting various taxes (evidently to the temple).

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a pillar in the south side of the veranda round the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1080, Bahudhānya, Āshāḍha, amāvāsyā, Monday. Probably A.D. 1158, June 27; but the week-day was Friday and not Monday. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 464]
cells.remarks: Records that Samundayan built the pavement of the temple for the merit of Irsvi Dasayan. The characters belong to about the 10th century A.D.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a pillar in the west side of the veranda round the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama year 49, Krōdhi, Vaiśākha, ba. ·4, Sunday = A.D. 1124, May 4, Sunday ; ·59. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 465]
cells.remarks: Seems to be of the same period. Records the gift of the pillar by Kōviḍaiyan of Perumponḍai.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a second pillar in the west side of the veranda round the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Seems to be of the same period. Records the gift of the pillar by Kōviḍaiyan of Perumponḍai.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a third pillar in the west side of the veranda round the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the 'Pillar (was) planted' by Gōvindan alias Ilangaiōdaraiyan. There is a standing figure with joined palms cut in relief in the centre of the inscription, which is evidently meant to represent the donor. The inscription belongs to about the 14th century A.D.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the east wall (right of entrance) of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift by the king of 2 vëli of tax-free land in Viragkumuda-nallur for offerings and maintenance of the service called Bukkaiyayan-sandhi in the temple of Pallikonda-Perumāl, from the 2₂ vëli of land for the maintenance of four priests conducting worship in the temple.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone built into the floor on the south side of the second prākāra of the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: A few letters at the end are lost. Records an agreement by the assembly of Nandikampa-chaturvēdimangalam in Pali-nādu, a sub-division of Paḍuvur-kōṭṭam, to feed certain asuōtios (visiting the village) daily, in return for a grant of 400 kuli of tax-free land made as dānapuram by a lady named Umaiyal.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the stone built into the floor on the south side of the second prākāra of the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple. †
cells.remarks: A few letters at the end are lost. Records a similar agreement with the same assembly by a certain Vaṇakkanaḍan alias Nambi of Mūrpati who endowed as dānapuram 2,000 kuli of land in the village and its hamlet Vaippur alias Arikulataka-chaturvēdimangalam, for feeding daily a specified number of persons versed in the Vedas.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the inner wall of the prākāra of the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple, right of entrance. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a gift of land to a certain Kouki Ramalingam by the king for some service in the temple of Pallikoṇḍa-Ranganāthasvāmi.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the outer wall of the gōpura of the Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple, left of entrance. †
cells.date: Śaka 1554, Durmati (wrong), Mesha, śu. 10, Wednesday, Makha.
cells.remarks: Records the hereditary grant of some land and a portion of the daily offered food in the temple to the Kaikkōmudalis of Pallikoṇḍai by the temple authorities, for the service of bearing the image of the god in processions.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south base of the central shrine in the Nāganāthēśvara temple in the same village (as Uttara-Rangandhā-svami temple). †
cells.remarks: Damaged and built in at the bottom. Seems to record the remission by the assembly of Nandikampa-Chaturvēdimaṅgalam, of the taxes on some land endowed for burning a lamp in the temple of Tirunāgīśvarattu-Dēvar by a certain individual (name lost), who paid a lump sum for the purpose.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west base of the central shrine in the Nāganāthēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Seems to record an agreement by the sumu assembly to remove from the tank every year to the extent of 20 kuḷi with the interest on a sum of money deposited with them by a resident of the village, for a lamp in the temple.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a pillar in the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Nāganāthēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the mukha-maṇḍapa was erected by Śelva Vāṇaraiyan, son of Amaṇi-Gaṅgaiyaraiyar.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the left door-jamb of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Nāganāthēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the ardha-maṇḍapa was built by a certain Karuvili Muttaraiyan.

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north and west bases of the Sōliyammaṉ temple in the village. †
cells.remarks: Portions lost. Seems to record some provision made by the residents of their village, for the celebration of the goddess Bhadrakāḷi of their village, by levying the watertax due from certain specified residents of the village. Near this inscription are found three more lines of writing of about the same period which record an agreement by the same assembly to maintain offerings and worship to the Bhaṭārar from the endowment made by Gōvindamārāya, son of Kōṭṭaiyār of Kaḷamūr, a member of the gaṇa (committee).

cells.location: Pallikonda, Vellore taluk, North Arcot district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up near a tank at Kaṇḍanēri, a hamlet of the village. †
cells.remarks: In modern characters. Records that (tank ?) is the gift of Dulavayi Bommayya-Nāyikkam, the daughter of a certain Gāṅgaiya of Vōlōr.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple
cells.remarks: Built in at the ends. Records a gift of land for the maintenance of the sacred bath on a certain day every month, for the burning of a perpetual lamp and for feeding a hundred brahmans on the Uttarāyaṇa and Dakshiṇāyaṇa days of the year in the temple of Śrīkailāsamuḍaiya-Mahādēva built by Sembiyan-Mahādēviyār at Sembiyanmahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmādēya in Aḷa-nāḍu on the southern bank. The lands were purchased by the queen for the purpose from two ladies, a daughter and her mother who respectively held the right of strīdhana and of disposal over the lands devolved upon them by the latter's husband.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift, by Uraṭṭayaṇ Śorabbaiyar alias Tribhuvena-Madēviyār, the queen of Madhurantakadēva alias Uttama-Chola, of 100 kāsu which was deposited with the Perumakka! of Srikailasam. From the interest on the amount certain offerings were to be made in the temple on the day of 'Tirukkeṭṭai in the month of Chittirai, which was the natal star of her mother-in-law Uđaiyapiraṭṭiyar Pirantakaṇ-Madēvadīgalar alias Śembiyaṇ-Madēviyār. The village is said to have been founded by the latter.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.date: Rājēndra— 8th year, Simha, Tuesday, Jyeshṭha and Tulā, Saturday, Ādēsha.
cells.remarks: Beginning built in. Records the remission by the assembly of the village, of the taxes due on a land granted by a resident, for the maintenance of a lamp in the temple. Ala-nādu in Arumolidēva-valanādu has been a b-division of Arumolidēva-valanādu. Records another remission by the same assembly of the taxes on some land granted by another individual for offerings and worship to the images of Īsabhuvahānavadēvar and of queen Sembiyan-madēvī-Pirāttiyār and to several other images in the temple for which no offerings had hitherto been made. Mentions Vikramaśōla-vadi.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in. Record a gift of 220 kalōṇju of gold by Arumolī Ariñjigaippiraṭṭi and . . . Kundavaiyar for similar offerings in the temple on the day of Keṭṭai in the month of Chittirai. The money was deposited with the Perumakka! who were 'bound by orders' (śāsanaṭaddha) to Kailasam.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning built in. Records a decision of the assembly which had met in the Śembiyaṇ-madēviya!-periyamaṇdapam in the village, to utilize the vellāṇveṭi tax derived from the dēvadāna lands of the temple of Ādityeśvaram-uđaiya-Mahadēva at Mogaṇur, the western hamlet of the village, for burning a twilight lamp in that temple.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north base of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Commences with the introduction poesarag etc. Seems to record the remission, by royal order, of the taxes on eone lands belonging to the temple of TiruveĹirukkai-Mabādēva for a lump payment of 100 kāsu made to the assembly of Śāṭṭiyakkudi. In the same place is another long introduction of an inscription ending with the regnal year of king Vijaya-Rajendra.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records a gift of certain lands for various offerings and worship in the temple built by Udaya-pirāttiyār Madhurāntakan-Mādēviyār alias Sembiyan Mahādēviyār, mother of Gaṇḍan-varshāntakdēvar alias Uttama-Chōladēva, by Uraiyān Sōrābhāyir alias Tribhuvana-Mādēviyār, queen of Uttama-Chōla, who purchased for the purpose some plots of land to supple-ment her own.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the north, west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end, and below the 2nd line. Begins with the introduction Svasti śrī, etc., and stops with the mention of the sub-division Vaḷḷuvakkōṭṭam of Aru-moḷidēva-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the north, west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. Stops with the mention of Aja-nādu in Arumolidēva-valanādu.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple, †
cells.remarks: Mention of Aḷa-nāḍu in Arumoḷidēva-vaḷanāḍu. Gives a detailed list of the articles required for worship, offerings and the sacred bath to the deity on all the saṅkrānti days of the year, for which provision was made by Uṛaiyūr-Soḻabbaṭṭar, the senior queen (of Uttama-Chōḷa).

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a grant of 150 kaḻañju of gold by a resident of Puṅgala-nāḍu to the temple, for feeding with the interest thereon certain persons on the day of Kēṭṭai in Chittirai, the natal star of Sembiyan-Mādēviyār, the mother of Uttama-Chōḷa.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a gold forehead-plato for the image of the deity by Paṭpan Dapatongiyar, a queen of Uttama-Chola.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a gold-handled fly-whisk for the deity by Pañchavap-Mahadēviyar, another queen of Parakēsarivarman alias Uttama-Choladēva.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift, by a lady (queen?) named Kanpapparasiyar alias Soppa-Mahadēviyar, of 507 kalañju with the interest on which some offerings had to be made to the deity on the day of Ketṭai in Chittirai, which was the birth day of Sembiyap-Madēvi the founder of the temple. The money was to be in charge of the 'Chaturvedibhatṭa-ttānapporumukka.'

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Portion at the end of the inscription is lost. Seems to re-cord the remission of taxes on some lands belonging to the temple by the assembly of the village.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end and bottom. Records a gift of a oney to be deposited with the 'Chaturvēdibhaṭṭa-tṭaṇapp-poruṇṇukkal' for the purpose mentioned in No. 492 above, by five queens of Uttama-Chōḷa, including Maḷapaḍi Teppuvaṉ-Mahādēviyār, and Aṉavaṉ-Mahādē-viyār, daughter of a certain Iruṅgōḷar.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to record an order of the assembly to the ūr-vāriyam committee.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the base of the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Records a gift of 590 kalañju of gold by Arurap-Ambulattadigajar, a queen of Uttama-Chola, and another gift by Uraṭṭayap-Sōrabbai alias Tribhuvapa-Madēviyar, for a similar purpose as in No. 492 and 494. The committee called 'Sasanabaddha-ohaturvedibhatṭa-ttānapporumukka.' to whom the gift had been made is stated to have been the creation of Sembiyap-Madēvi herself.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the articles such as a golden pot, a forehead plate and some gold flowers, together with their weights, which were presented to the temple by the mother of Uttama-Cōḷa in the month of Māsi of the same year.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a detailed list of the several ornaments presented to the temple.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the mandapa in front of the central shrine in the Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the temple was renovated by Uttamavēdap-perumāḷ at the instance of the Periyaṇḍār and records the grant of a kaḍam of paddy each on every vēli of land.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of the Chandravāra shrine in Kailāsanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the assembly of the village decided to hold their meetings for the conduct of the grāma-kāryam and kaḍamakkāryam only in the day-time, since the night meetings consumed oil in excess of the quantity sanctioned for the lighting of the hall at nights, and not to re-elect the old members for the assembly until after five years.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the Chandravāra shrine. †
cells.remarks: Records the issue with all privileges to a certain stone-mason called Mūvēndavēḷār, alias Vīra-Pāṇḍya-Āchāriyan, by the tanattār of the temple who had assembled in a meeting in the hall called Iruṅguḷēra-Perumāḷ-tiruk-kavaṇam.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inside the second gōpura, left of entrance, of the Ātmārthasvāmi temple at Avadayarkoil, Arantangi-taluk, Tanjore district.
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land by two residents of Kaṇḍiyūr to the temple of Avuḍaiya-kōyil-uḍaiya-nāyaṉār, through the agent Parādēsimuṭṭirai Vaṇḍāva-Puṇḍāran, for the requirements of worship to the deity in the Kanakasabhā-maṇḍapa in the temple. Tiruppurandurai is also called Pavitramāṇikkam-ohaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inside the main gōpura of Ātmārthasvāmi temple (left of entrance). †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a village called Kaḷḷaṇḍavayal by several male and female members of two families of Tiruppurandurai for the conduct of the gurupūjai in the temple to Vēṇadēva-Perumāḷ, also called in the inscription the Tiruppanikkal-rājā of the temple.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inside the main gōpura of the Ātmārthasvāmi temple at Avadayarkoil, Arantangi-taluk, Tanjore district (left of entrance). †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of 30 ēli of land by the grandsons of a certain Piḷḷaikkāḷavār, a resident of the village, to Vāmadēva-Paṇḍāram who was doing the tiruppaṇi in the śrībhaṇḍāram of the temple, towards the gurupūjai service performed by him.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inside the main gōpura of the Ātmārthasvāmi temple at Avadayarkoil, Arantangi-taluk, Tanjore district (left of entrance). †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land for worship in the Apaṭsahāyar-Pērambalam, by Kaṇḍappadēvar of Ayiravāy-aḍaiyappaḍar of Servappa Viśālapadēvar, son of Sarvappa Viśālapadēvar, one of the servant of Sūrakkuḍi, after purchasing the same from a servant of the mahājana. Mentions a coin called 'durai-minnal-poṇ'.

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inside the main gōpura of the Ātmārthasvāmi temple at Avadayarkoil, Arantangi-taluk, Tanjore district (left of entrance). †
cells.date: Śaka 1539, Piṅgaḷa, Vaikāśi 26. [date-calculation appendix, No. 506: Śāka 1539, Piṅgala, Vaikāsi 25 May correspond to A.D. 1617, May 22.]

cells.location: Sembiyanmahādēvi, Nēgapatam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: In the main gōpura of the Ātmārthasvāmi temple at Avadayarkoil, Arantangi-taluk, Tanjore district (right of entrance). †

cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land made tax-free to the temple of Vinnagar-Emberumaṇ by Kandaṇ Udaiyaṇjeydaṇ alias Gathgēyaṇ of Niyamam in Tenṇarruppōkko, for the daily offerings to the images of Manavālalyar and his consort set up in the temple by a merchant of Alakapuri alias Sembiyanarāyanapuram.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the temple in ruins †
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes in favour of the temple by the person mentioned in No. 16 above on the land purchased by a merchant of Kalaiyakalap-perunteruvu and on the land granted as tiruvidaiyāṭṭam by two private individuals.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the temple in ruins †
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a remission of taxes by the assembly of Kanaṇađu alias Virudarajabuyathkara-valaṇađu on a land at Ūrñiyūr granted as tiruvidaiyātīfam to the temple by two private individuals.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the temple in ruins †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for mid-day service on the day of Uttiram, the natal star of Vīra-Vīra-Nāyaṉār, son of Vīra-yākyadēvar.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the temple in ruins †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land in Ilaiyattakkudi as tiruvidaiyātīfam for the offerings and other expenses to the god by the same chief.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the temple in ruins †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. Seems to register a gift of land, free of taxes, by Kandaṇ-Āludaiyaṇ alias Kalvayil-Nađalvaṇ mentioned in No. 16 above.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the right door-jamb of the Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the two door-posts, the two stone steps and the two puliyadi stones were the gift of a brahman named Perumal-Dēvapillai.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab lying near the Vishnu temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to register a remission of taxes on a land purchased by a certain Pillaiyal assembly.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of the Adikesava-Perumal temple in the same village (as Vishnu temple). †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of use by the residents (urar) of Ilaiyattakkudi on a land granted as tirunamattukkani by Kandan Qualaiyuran alias Kalingattarayar of Valavānallur, to the temple of Periyanachi-Vinnagar-Emberuman for worship and offerings to the image of the deity set up by himself.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the Adikesava-Perumal temple in the same village (as Adikesava-Perumal temple) †
cells.date: 39th year, Makarn, śu. trayōdaci, Friday, Aśvati.
cells.remarks: Stones lost in the middle. Registers a similar remission of taxes on another land granted as tirunamattukkani for the same purpose by the same donor.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the Adikesava-Perumal temple. †
cells.date: 39th year, Makarn, śu. trayōdaci, Friday, Aśvati.
cells.remarks: Registers another grant of land by the same person to the same temple.

cells.location: Ilayāttangudi, Tiruppattur taluk, Ramanathapuram district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the Adikesava-Perumal temple †
cells.date: 39th year, Makarn, śu. trayōdaci, Friday, Aśvati.
cells.remarks: Stone containing ends of lines 1-4 lost. Registers the order of the assembly of Iraṇiyūr about the land granted as tirunāmattukkāni to the temple.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the Adikesava-Perumal temple †
cells.remarks: Registers the order of the assembly of Ilaiyattakkudi in Kaļayal-nādu regarding the gift of land mentioned in No. 34 above.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the west wall of the Ganesa shrine in the Kailasanathasvami temple in the same village (as Adikesava-Perumal temple). †
cells.remarks: Stones lost. Records a remission of taxes on the village Singalanallur sold by Kandan Aludaiyan alias Kaļayal-Nādālyan to the goddess Tirukamakottam-Nachchiyar set in the temple of Kaļayallam-udaiya-Nayinār in Kaļayal-nādu.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the south wall of the shrine in the Kailasanathasvami temple in the same village (as Ganesa shrine). †
cells.remarks: Stones lost. Registers sale of ground of house-site made tax-free to two persons, by the assembly of Kuļā-[dokarapuram] in Kaļayal-nādu.

cells.location: Ilaiyattangudi, Tirup-pattur taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Kailasanathasvami temple in the same village (as Kailasanathasvami temple) †
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes by the assembly of Neisayil in consideration of money received by them on the goddess Singalankantakainallur, sold to the goddess by Kaļayil-Na'ālyar.

cells.location: Ilayāttangudi, Tiruppattur taluk, Ramanathapuram district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up on the tank-bund in front of the Pathapasvami temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: States that the channel running to the east of the Pattavu-svamigal-tank is called Arijuda-Perumal.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a slab set up on the tank-bund in front of the Pathapasvami temple in the same village (as Kailasanathasvami temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Registers an order of Malavarayan granting land in Vikramarama-valanadu for the maintenance of a matha called 'Muludumvallavan-tirumandapam'.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the Ayyarvar temple (in ruins) †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to register an order of Kaļayal-Nadal-var to the nesamuly of Kuļattur alias Vanavamadevi-nallur granting a fresh sale-deed of some lands in the village belonging to it in place of the old document which had become crumbeled by age. Mentions the 13+ 7th year, apparently of Kuļasēkhara.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the right door-jamb of the Ayyarvar temple. †
cells.remarks: States that this door and the step were the gifts of Ponnan Paḍaiyan alias Tirujñānasambandar of Kaļattur.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone set up at the entrance into the Ayyarvar temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to fix the rate of taxes payable on some lands situated in the two villages Tinneraikudi and Erumbukudi alias Jalavachakanallur in Kirāṇi-nādu, granted to a Siva temple.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On stones built into the south wall of the mandapa in front of the central shrine in the Subrahmanya temple in the same village (as Ayyarvar temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to register the order of the assembly of Mudikondapandyapuram in Teŋkalai-nādu remitting the taxes due on certain lands belonging to the temple of Tiruhohivaman udaiya-Nayanar in their village to provide for offerings and other expenses to the god. Refers to Periys-Nayanar Vikrama-Pandyadeva in whose time the lands had been endowed to the temple.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the wall of the mandapa in front of the central shrine in the Subrahmanya temple in the same village (as Subrahmanya temple) †
cells.remarks: States that this represents the length of the land measure called 'Kolkudīngi'. The writing is engraved by the side of a mark which measures exactly three feet from another mark to its left. It is however possible that the intervening space might have been greater since the walls have been re-built.

cells.location: Kovanoor, Sivaganga taluk, Ramnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the east wall of the prakara of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a gift of some tax-free land to the temple after purchasing the same from Jayankondasolan Kalaval-Nadalvar. Mentions the measuring rod 'Vira-Pandyan-kol'. Refers to a brother-in-law of the king? by name Alagapperumal Jayankonda-

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the Tiruvaruldivara temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records an assignment by the king at the request of Malavarayan, of a portion of the taxes due on the lands at Irāśaiyanallur for the maintenance of the service called 'Sundara-Pandyan-sandi' to the images of the god and goddess and of Sōmesvaram-Udaiyar in the temple. Mentions the throne called Malavarāyan in the hall of the palace at Madura east of Madurōdaya-vaļanādu.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On three sides of a pillar in the Tiruvaruldivara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the redemption from mortgage of a certain land belonging to the temple of Tiruvalandurai-udaiyar at Perumbalur in Rajarajenallur in Tirt-tihaippur-kōrram by Aļa[gan]-Vaḍugar alias Kalinga-rāyar, a servant at the door of Kalingarayana-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On another pillar in the Tiruvaruldivara temple. †
cells.remarks: States that this pillar was the gift of Sambandan Paļi-yālvān alias Mulikkunnāyakan, a merchant residing at the Avvaipperunteruvu of Sompoŋmāri.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a third pillar in the Tiruvaruldivara temple. †
cells.remarks: States that this pillar was the gift of Sātteppillai, a dancing-girl residing in the tirunada-vīļagam of the temple of Tiruvadaṇḍai-uḍaiya-Nāyaṉār in Rājēndra-nallūr.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a beam in the Tiruvaruldivara temple †
cells.remarks: States that in times of distress, Amrāpatikattār Alagiya Śōkkar of Aruvīmānagaram and others effected repairs, constructed a tuṛu and made arrangements for worship in the temple of Tiruvalanda-īśuram-Uḍaiyār at Kājara-nallūr in Tirukkāppūr-kūṟṟam and that subsequently the trustees of the temple got back by purchase for the worship to god, the dēvadāna land which had passed out of the possession of the temple.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the door-jamb of the entrance into the central shrine of Tillaivāṇēśvara temple in the same village (as Tiruvaruldivara temple). †
cells.remarks: States that a certain Toṇḍiyār-muṇ-chief of Toṇḍi set up in his name the door-post in the temple.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the left door-jamb in the mahā-maṇḍapa of the Tiruvaruldivara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged at the end. Seems to record the provision made for the daily worship (nityōtsava) to the god in the temple of Perumbālūr-Nāyaṉār at Palūr alias Hajarū-nallūr in Tirukkāppūr-kūṟṟam by a certain Saḷi-Kaṭṭaṉ alias Aṇḍāṉ-kūttan-Kāḷi-Kīḷai-Vēḷāṉ of Naṇyil in the same division.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a beam in the ceiling of the Tiruvaruldivara temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to register a gift of land, free of taxes uḻadēvadāna for offerings, etc., to the god of Perumbālūr at Rājara-nallūr. Mentions the measuring rod 'Sundara-Pāṇḍyan-kōl' measuring 24 feet in length. Mentions the headman of Aḍukkoṭṭai (f) in Kavuṇūr in Aṇuṇṇūr-kūṟṟam.

cells.location: Radhanur, Tiruvadanai taluk, Remnad district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the door-jamb of the entrance into the Vighnēśvara shrine in same temple.
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Seems to record some gift to this shrine by the kaikkōḷas of Madurai for the merit of Aravā-yaṉ Uyyavanda-āḷvār Poyyāppū-Chōḷa-nallūr of Kappūr alias Ulagalaṇḍa-nallūr in Mutturruk-kūṟṟam.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the north wall of the third prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Stones lost at the beginning and end. Register a gift of 8 vēli of land as areha-nābhōga, free of taxes, for worship to the image of Tirukkadavār-Nāyaṇar in the temple of the god Tillaiyali-Isvaram-Udaiyar at Tillaiyalinallūr in Kurumbar-naṇu by the big assembly of Tirukkadavār.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the wall of the third prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a remission of taxes (kāsukōla-iraiyili) on certain lands belonging to the temple for 26th kāu received by the assembly of Tirukkadavār in Rajanārayana-valausadu that met in the hall called 'Tiruchchirgambala-Vēlaik-kaṇaṇ-tirumandapa' in the temple of Kalakaladēvar.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the wall of the third prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.date: 5th year, Kumbha, gu. dvadasi, Thursday, Punarpāsam.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Incomplete and stones lost. Gives a list of some more lands for which remission was granted for the same assembly in favour of both the temples.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the west wall of the sēvai prākāra.
cells.date: 4th year, Vriśobika, gu. daśami, Monday, Revati.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction purīṣa etc., Registers a sale of ₹ mā of land by Karunakaran of Sendiram, a member of the Alingaṇam of Virudaraja-bhayanikarachohaturvedimatgalam in Mangi-nādu a subdivision of Virudarajabhayanikara-vajunadu, to Sattamallan-Mudikondar alias VaṇakOvaraiyar, residing at Valaiyūr alize Sunbai, on the northern bank of the river Pennai, in Vāṇagappadi alias Raje.drasōla-valanādu.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the wall of the sēvai prākāra †
cells.date: 4th year, Vriśobika, gu. daśami, Monday, Revati.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a similar sale of land by Ilaiya Sri-Vasudeva-BhaTTan of Kundūr, another member of the assembly to the same individual.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the sēvai prākāra †
cells.date: 4th year, Vriśobika, gu. daśami, Monday, Revati.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a similar sale of land to the same person by Kiraiji P'amōdira Tirumānī-Saran, another member of the same assembly.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the sēvai prākāra †
cells.date: 4th year, Vriśobika, gu. daśami, Monday, Revati.
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Unfinished. Registers a similar sale of land to the same person by Sīrāma-Saharan of Nadadūr, another member of the assembly.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the sēvai prākāra †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the introduction svasti srī, etc. Seems to record a remission of taxes by the assembly (name lost) for 304 kāśu received from the temple of Tiruvavadurai-Udaiyār.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the sēvai prākāra †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Has a portion of the introduction commencing with the words svasti śrī; ... of Vikrama-Chōla. Seems to record the purchase of a land (for the temple?) out of the money endowed by a certain Dēvan-Jahonavēdīvaran the headman of Mattūr for the daily feeding of the dēvār of the Pañchanelivānan-maDam situated in the street adjoining the temple. Refers to a land granted for the maint nance of a naTa-śālai of the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the south wall of the prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones lost in the beginning. Records the remission of taxes (kāṣukollā-ijaiyili) by the assembly, on a land granted to the temple after purchase, by a merchant of the place who was a native of Siruvaṇdūr.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai †
cells.place: On the wall of the prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Built in at the end. Begins with the introduction puraṇa mula kā, etc. Registers a remission of taxes (kāśuko!lā-iyaiyili for a lump sum of 100 kaśu received by them on 2 vēli of land given after purchase by a certain Pavalakkunpu-Periyā, a woman waiting on queen Mukkōkkilānadigal to the temple of Maṅgalēsvaram-udaiya-Mahadeva at Kulōttungasōlanallūr, a virabhōga village of the kaikkōlas of Gāṅgaikondasōlapuram, by the assembly that met in the temple of Tiruvaraiudaiya-Mahadeva at Salukkikulakalanallīr, a hamlet of Ulaguy-yakondasōlach-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Mērka-naḍo, a division of Virudarajabhayaṅkara-vala-naḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.date: [4th] year, Kumbha, su. dvādasi, Wednesday, Ani-sham.
cells.remarks: Written below the 6th line and portion lost at the right end. Mentions the god and his consort TirukkamkkōTTam-udaiya-Pariyanthōhaiyar. Seems to record the transfer of a land belonging to the temple of Vikrama-Chōlēsvara to that of Tirumāligai-Subrahmanya-Pillaiyār situated in the street Vikramaśōla-iruvadi at Tiruvavadurai.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.date: 3rd year Mahāra, śu., prathamā, Friday, Āvittam.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction puraṇa mula kā, etc., Registers a remission of taxes (kāśuko!lā-iyaiyili) for 716 kaśu on about 13 cēli of land set apart after purchase for feeding brahmans, tapasvins and the destitute in the feeding house called 'Peruntiruvāṭti' founded by the sēnapati Sankkaran Ambalaṅkōyilkondān alias Anantapalar of Ilaṅgarikudi in Pēravū-naḍu in the same valanaḍu, by the assembly of Ulaguyyakkondasōlach-chaturvēlimaṅgalam that met in the Sankkaradēva-Tirumaṇdapa situated in front of the temple of the god Tiruvavaduturai-Udaiyar in Tireimūr-naḍu, a division of Uyyakkondar-valanaḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvadaṇḍuvai
cells.place: On the wall of the prākāra of the Gōmukhtēśvara temple †
cells.date: [2]7th year, Kanni, ba. daśamī, Monday, pūśam.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction puraṇa mula kā, etc. Incomplete, being built in below the 13th line. Mentions the village Kulōttungasōlanallūr granted as virabhōga to the Agambadi-Kaikkōlas of the Śirudapam who were natives (F) of Me[r]ka-naḍu in Virudarajabhayaṅkara-valanaḍu.

cells.location: Anāngur
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple
cells.remarks: Seems to register the royal assignment of certain tax-free lands at Vēlānnayakamangalam a dēvadāna village of the temple of Agastyēsvara-Mahādēva at Anāngur in Merkkondaśōla-valanādu, to the temple for the maintenance of TiruvaLandor and Araisiūr for digging irrigation channels from the Kāvēri. The royal secretary Rājanārāyanam-Māvandavēlaiyārugas one of the signatories.

cells.location: Anāngur †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction pū-mādu puṇara etc. Re-giters a remission of taxes for 40 kāśu received as irai-kāval by the big assembly of Aṅgaṇūr, a brahmādēya in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu, during the 10th year of Kō-Rāja-kēsarivarman, to be met in the temple of Tirunārāyaṇa-Piṇiyattalvār, on half a vēli of land which had been sold by it to the temple of Tiruvagastīśvaram-Uḍaiyār.

cells.location: Anāngur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple †
cells.remarks: Gives a list and extent of the dēvadāna lands belonging to the temple of Tiruvagastīśvaram-Uḍaiyār at Tiruvāḷangāḍu, a brahmādēya in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu, in the 10th year of Kō-Rāja-kēsarivarman, and at Paṇanguḍi granted by Sembiyamādēvi-Piṇiyattār, the mother of Uttama-Chōḷa, who constructed this stone temple for the god.

cells.location: Anāngur †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the royal order at the request of Viḷḷavarāyan to the assembly of Jagadēkavīrach-chaturvēdimangalam in Vīrarājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, a village adjacent to Aṅgaṇūr, remitting the taxes on the lands given as dēvadāna and belonging to the shrine of Veḷḷai-Vināyagabhūram-Uḍaiyār in the temple. Rājēndraśōḷa-Mūvēndavēḷān, the royal secretary, figures as one of the signatories.

cells.location: Anāngur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged in the middle. Records a gift of gold for burning a lamp in the temple at Tiruvāḷangāḍu, a brahmādēya in Teralu-nāḍu, by a certain Ādittan, a resident of the village of Uṭṭattūr in Uṭṭattūr-nāḍu of the village. Records a gift of 10 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple by a resident of Peḷaikuḍi, a brahmādēya in Amara-nāḍu.

cells.location: Anāngur †
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Agastyēsvara temple †
cells.remarks: Middle portion of the first line built in. Seems to record the sale to the temple, of the right of collecting taxes from the lands (the details are broken) sold to certain residents of the śiruvai-dēvadānam of the temple of Tiruvāḷangāḍ-Uḍaiyār at Vikramaśōḷan-Allūr since they had been in payment of dues on this land.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Built in the middle. Records the confirmation of the royal order mentioned in No. 81 below at the request of Koṅgārāyan about a grant of land at Sutta-malli, a brahmādēya in the same nāḍu, including the 8½ vēli presented by himself as tirumaṭṭukkāṇi to the god.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in the middle. Records the confirmation of the royal order mentioned in No. 81 below at the request of Koṅgārāyan about a grant of land at Sutta-malli, a brahmādēya in the same nāḍu, including the 8½ vēli presented by himself as tirumaṭṭukkāṇi to the god.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the south, east and north walls of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in the middle. Begins with the introduction pū-mādu aruḷiya etc. Registers the royal order regarding the same grant of land.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the walls of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers the royal order confirming, at the instance of Kongarayan, the grant of land as tirunāmattukkāni for a flower-garden to the temple made in the 11th year of Kulōttunga-Chōladēva who remitted the tolls.' The royal secretary Rājanārāyana-Māvandavēlaiyan appears as one of the signatories.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu
cells.place: On the walls of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records the restoration, after due enquiries by the officers Vāndarājan, Nulambadarājan and others, to the temple at Tiruvalangādu in Vikrāmasōla-janappālar, in Jayan-kondasōla-valanādu, of a portion of the tirunāmattukkāni land, belonging to the temple, which had however been wrongly claimed as the garden-land belonging to the god at TiruvaVadaparai. Mentions Kongarayan as the person through whom the matter was taken to the notice of the king.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the east and north walls of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the permission granted to the temple of Tiruvalan-dura-Udaiyār to utilise the yield of the trees planted in a plot adjacent to the temple ground for providing pro-viding oil for lamps (to be burnt in the temple). The royal secretary mentioned in No. 82 above figures as a signatory.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maNdaPa in front of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. Registers a grant of land by purobase for burning lamps during the services before the image of Visvēšvaradēva set up by Monpai-Āpđar alius Rajaraja-Tafājanātū-Mūvendaveļaṇ in the temple of Tiruvalangađu-Udaiyar.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the wall of the maNdaPa in front of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers the order of Raļappālarayan granting about 9½ vēli of land as tax-free tirunāmattukkāni to the temple of Tiruvalangađu-Udaiyar, as compensation for 10½ vēli of the temple lands acquired by the king in the villages Suttavali-chaturvēdimangalam and Kavanūr alius Janaparipalapuram, for founding a Brahmaya agruhāra called Irumarabun-tuyyaperumaļ-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the north wall of the maNdaPa in front of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Registers the royal order at the request of Vayilaiharayan to engrave on the temple walls the title of the deed for 27 veLi of land granted as tirunāmattukkāni to the god.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the wall of the maNdaPa in front of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a similar royal order at the request of Vayilaiharayan to engrave on the temple walls the extent of the lands enjoyed tax-free as ūrkkādi-iraiyīti by the god, in accordance with the decision of both the assemblies of the village, viz., mahāchabai and ūr. Rājanārāyana-Māvandavēlaiyān figures as one of the signatories.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the wall of the maNdaPa in front of the shrine in Vaṭāraṇyēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers tax-free gifts, by the residents of Muḍikoṇḍa-śōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Jayaṅkoṇḍa-śōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, of lands as arkki-iriyiḷi in [A]mbāpurattār alias Nakki-Aura-chaturvēdimangalam in Uyyakkonḍār vaḷanāḍu and Pāppakuḍi in Gōyappaṭṭika-vaḷanāḍu to the temple at Vikkiramachōḷa-Allūr.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the east wall of the verandah round the central shrine of the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift by purchase of 36 persons labonrers (mađa-ađimai) to the temple of Tiruvalańgađu-Udaiyar by Vayiradarayar, the headman of Aļūr.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the wall of the verandah round the central shrine of the Agastyēsvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers another gift by purchase of three persons by the same headman to the temple for service as maḍa-palli.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the east and south walls of the verandah round the central shrine of the Agastyēsvara temple, †
cells.date: 24th year, Rishabha, ba. saptami, Wednesday, Sadayam.
cells.remarks: Stones misplaced. Registers a declaration by the trustees of the temple of Tiruvālaṅgāḍu-Uḍaiyār as its property at Vikkiramaśōḷa-Allūr in Paravūr-nāḍu a subdivision of Uyyakkonḍār-vaḷanāḍu, of 14 vēli and odd of land made up of plots presented to the temple by a Brahman resident of Muḍikoṇḍaśōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Naḷḷāṟṟūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Vīraśōḷa-vaḷanāḍu, and of lands purchased by them as tirumaḍa-viḷāgam and the money realized by the sale of certain temple jewels.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the west wall of the second prākāra of the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.date: 10th year, Kanni, ba. saptami, Friday, Rōhiṇi.
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes due on 86 kuḷi of land belonging to Vaṇṇāramāḍa-Aṇḍān-mēṭam by the trustees of the temple of Tiruvālaṅgāḍu-Uḍaiyār at the instance of Piḷḷai Āvantiyarāyar.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the wall of the second prākāra of the Agastyēsvara temple †
cells.remarks: Stones lost in the middle. Seems to register the royal order permitting the temple authorities to punish and bring back to temple those persons who had been presented to the temple by Vayiradarāyar and his wife and those who had been purchased by the temple itself, since these had absconded from their work.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged in the middle. Records the royal order according permission to engrave on the temple walls the gift of lands made to the servants purchased for the temple for service by Vayiradarāyar [and] his [wife].

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: On the north wall of the prākāra of the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.date: 12th year, Dhanus, śu. ēkādaśi, Monday, Kārttikai.
cells.remarks: Beginning of the introduction lost. Registers a sale of 119 kuli of house site for 1804 kāis to Āndar Vidivitankap-Perumal, one of the maṭhādhipatis of Vanpāramadēva-Āndar-mađam by the trustees of the temple of Tiruvalańgađu-Udaiyar.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: In the gōpura of the Agastyēsvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives the length of the measuring rod Ulagalandān as compared with that mentioned in the inscriptions of the temple of Rājarājēśvaram-Uḍaiyār at Tañjāvūr.

cells.location: Tiruvalangāḍu †
cells.place: In the gōpura of the Agastyēsvara temple (outside) †
cells.remarks: The inscription is engraved by the side of a standing figure with hands joined against the chest in a worshipping posture. States that it is Vagīśar, the headman of Maṇalūr.

cells.location: Kuttalam
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Built at the beginning. Commences with the introduction Tirumagal-pōla etc. Registers a gift of land for feeding Śivayōgins at the mid-day service in the temple of Tirukkarrali-uḍaiya-Mahādēva by Śivadhanmā-kēraṇ[a]n Rājanārāyaṇa-vaḷanāḍu for the prosperity of the king's arms. The donor made a further grant of 12 kāśu towards the annual payment of taxes on the land.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On the south and east walls of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a royal gift of the village Kavirimalai, free of taxes, as decided with the boundaries clearly marked in detail, to the temple of Tirukkarrali-Mahādēva through the assembly of Tiruvaiḷundūr-nāḍu. Portion of the village had been confiscated as esḷing-engai from a certain Nāgan Aḍita-Piḍaran for a certain crime (not specified) committed by him and the rest had been acquired by purchase or exchange from several individuals.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On the south, east and north walls of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Regins with the introduction § ... etc. Seems to register a gift of land, free of all taxes, made in the 8rd year of the king for conducting certain festivals in the temple of Sonnavarariyum-Mahadéva at Vingunirttirutturutti in Tiruvalundór-nađu on the king's birthday, and of the taxes due from certain villages amounting to 80 kús a year for the festival in the asterism Tiruvadirai in the month of Margali in the temple.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On the walls of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Tirumagal-pōla etc. Registers an agreement by a number of brāhmaṇas of Tiruvaiḷundūr, a brāhmaṇadēya-nāḍu to feed the brāhmaṇas during the midday service of the god Soṇṇavararivar, with the interest on 25 kāśu received by them from Veyyāḍan Aḍavallān, a merchant of Guṇaikkoṇḍaśōlapuram, who made this endowment for the prosperity of the king's arms.

cells.place: On the south, east and north walls of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. States that the temple was constructed by Sembiyan-Mahadéviyar, the molhar of Uttama-Chola, and registers the provision made by her by gifts of land for offerings, worship museo and other expones, and for reoiting the Sama, Taitiiriya and Chandoga Samavéda in the temple.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On the north wall of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built at the end. Registers a sale of 8 mā of land made tax-free to the temple of Tirukkaṭṭali-Mahādēva at Viṅguntirutturutti by the assembly of Villaṉ-Madēvich-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brāhmaṇa in Tiru-vaḷundūr-nāḍu, a division of Uyyakkonḍār-vaḷanāḍu, on payment of 48 kāśu.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Tirumagal-pōla etc. Records a gift of 90 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp to the image of Poṟṟāmarai-Viṭaṅkar in the temple of Bōgavarīśvarar at Viṅguntirutturutti, a dēvadāna in Tiru-vaḷundūr-nāḍu, a division of Uyyakkonḍār-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Kuttalam
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Uktavēdīśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Begins with the same introduction. Records a gift of 360 kaḻañju of gold by Vīraṇalpaṟṟan Kuṭṭaṭṭali, a Vaḷañjai-kōḷaikkāran residing at Kāvirinallūr, a brāhmaṇa in Tiru-vaḷundūr-nāḍu for conducting the midnight worship of the god Soṅgaravarīśvarar from the interest on the amount which was invested with Eḍuṭṭaḍam-Seyyapadām alias Tirutturutti-Piḷḷai-chan attached to the temple.

cells.location: Kuttalam †
cells.place: On a slab near the tank in the Uktavēdīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the outer compound walls of the goddess shrine, the gōpura and the street leading to the temple of ...śvara at Tirutturutti-puram, were the gifts of Pippali Chidambara-Dīkṣitar.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Maṅgaḷēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers an agreement made by the śirudhanam of Tiru-rōḷaikkuḍi in Gaṅgaikoṇḍa-Chōḷachaturvēdimaṅgalam, a member of the āḷugaṇam of the village, for the interest on 30 kāśu received by them from the latter. Records also another agreement made by the same persons in the 27th year (of the same king's predecessor) to provide rice for the midnight service to the stone image of Kahaśēva dēva from the interest on 60 kaḻam of iḍaly received by them from Gōvinda-Kramavittan of Kuṇḍūr.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that this stone was the gift of Amarṇīti-Nakkan of Aṉṉiyūr, the headman of Kohaiyūr.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that this Durgā (image) was the gift of [Alaṉ]-Bala-dēva alias Pāṭṭinēśōbhara-Pallavaraiyaṉ of Neṟkuppai in Tiru-vaḷundūr-nāḍu. The inscription is engraved near the niche intended for this goddess, but the image is now missing.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 96 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp to the god Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi-uḍaiyār, on behalf of Vēḷimakkan, a merchant of Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi-nāḍu on the northern bank, by his two sons.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes by the assembly of Viḍelvidugu-chaturbvēdimangalam, a brāhmaṇēya in Vadak-Kurukkai-nādu on the lands purchased for burning a perpetual lamp before the god and for bringing water from the Kāvēri for the sacred bath of the deity, by a certain Aiyan Māraṅgāṇ alias Vīraśēkhara Mūvendavēlan of Guṇamalappāḍi in Naļļārrūr-nādu.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of a silver vessel weighing 30 kaļañju, by the same person to offer water to the god during worship.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xix||107" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIX, No. 107</button>; <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxii|ii|14" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXII Pt II, No. 14</button>

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records another gift by the same person of a silver vessel weighing 400 kaļañju for holding offerings to the god.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers an agreement made by the Sivabrāhmaṇas to provide offerings to the god Liṅgapurandarēva every midday, with the interest on 17 kaśu received by them from a certain lady residing in the village.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiii||73" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIII, No. 73</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by the assembly of Murugavēlmal-galam, a brāhmaṇēya in Kurukkai-nāḍu on the northern bank, to the trustees of the temple for three services, sounding the kēļam and beating the gōng during the śrībali offerings to Mangala-Nakkar in the temple of Mahādēvar.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiii||99" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIII, No. 99</button>

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land made tax-free by the assembly, by Pāradiyan [P]uliguḍaiyan of Murugavēl-maṅgalam, for offerings to the deity in the Naḍuvil-srikōyil (temple) in the same village.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the central shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Pugaluḍaiyān etc. Registers an agreement made to a certain lady of Sāmbi-yan-Kāuḍaiyār by four Sivabrāhmaṇas of the temple of Tirumankai-Mahādēva at Gaṅgikoṇḍa-chōla-chaturbvēdimangalam in Kurukkai-nāḍu, a subdivision of Virudarājabhayankara-vaļanādu to burn a twilight lamp before the consort of the god Maṅgala-Nambi.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the north and west bases of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones peeled away at the right end. Begins with the introduction Puvalarudaiya ... etc. Records a remission of taxes on lands belonging to the temple for a lamp sum received by it from the assembly of Gangikoṇḍaśōla-chaturbvēdimangalam in Kurukkai-nāḍu, a sub-division of Rājēndrasiṅga-vaļanāḍu

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the north, west and south walls of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Swācālas etc. Gives a detailed description of the tax-free lands endowed for flower-gardens and for the maintenance of the śribali to the god Tiruverudupađi-Mahadēva, in Kađalaṅguđi, also known as Vidēvidṅgudōvich-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Kuṇukkai-nādu, a sub-division of Rajendra-śirṇha-valanađu, in the [2]0th, 24th and 27th years of Rajarajakēsarivarman alias Rajarajadēva by the residents of Kađalaṅguđi, Iđaiyarą and Iāndūr in the same nādu, of Āluṅguđi in Nallarrūr-nādu and of Kođalor in Peravar-nādu, a division of Uyyukkondar-vulanađu. Also recordn a gift by his queen Artuwojīdēviyar] made in the 2nd year of Rajendra-Cboļadēva of 50 cows of which only 26 remained in the 5th year.

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the west wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land after purchasing it tax-free from the assembly of Viḍēviḍungōviḍ-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya in Naḷḷūr-nāḍu on the north side (of the river) by a certain Naṇādēsiya Eṟuḷattapaḍa Muṭṭeṭṭuppaṟa[l] for burning a perpetual lamp before the Koḷḷappuramaḷ [Naṭarāja] at Tiruvēḷvikkuḍi in Viḍēviḍungō-chaturvēdi-maṅgalam a brahmadēya in Kurukkai-nāḍu on the other bank of the river.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that the stone-post was the gift of Maḷḷa-Naṅgai, wife of Vīranarapa-Pallavaraiyar.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the bases of the west and south walls of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged in the middle. Begins with the introduction svasti śrī etc. Registers remission of taxes on 4 mā of land by the assembly (name lost) in favour of the god Tirukkaṟṟaḷi-Mahādēva at Tiruvēḷvikkuḍi in Gaṅgaikoṇḍaśōḷa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Naḷḷūr-nāḍu, a sub-division of Rājēndrachōḷa-vaḷanāḍu for 7 kāśu received by them from the temple treasury.

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the south wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 36 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp before the god Tiruvēlvikkuđi-Udaiyar by Korran Kūttan alias Sembiyan Ārkkatṭu-Veļan, the headman of Ārkkađu in Ārkkatṭuk-kūrram.
cells.also: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxxii|ii|16" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXXII Pt II, No. 16</button>

filters.also: Also in another book we hold

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Mentions a gift of 2 kāśu to the temple by Paṇṇāyan Kūḍanḍan, one of the Kaikkōḷas who held the iḷaiyaḍi (sword?).

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that this stone was the gift of a certain Śamidan.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: A letter lost at the beginning of each line. States that the structure up to the kal-padai and 14 stones were constructed by a certain Tiru-vaiyā[ṟu]-yōgi of Naḷḷūr.

cells.location: Tiruvilakkudi †
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a silver pitcher (kalakam) weighing 142 kalañju to the temple of Tiruvelvikkudi-Ályar by queen Pirantakan-Mádévadigalar alias Sembiyan-Mahádéviyár.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: The inscription is damaged by the side of the Dakshināmūrti image. States that the image was the gift of a certain Kada[ra]joh-ōngan, a servant of the Valanjiyar community.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records a gift of land to Tiruvēlvikkudi-Bhatarar by one Gunashīla Vāngavan, a merchant residing in Virakēralapērantēru.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that the temple was built by the members of the Valanjiyar and the ligai-Avintataihingovar communities and the rest of it by a certain Tiruvēlvikkudi-Nambi alias Tiruvayirand-yōgyar and his son Śrīka[ra]m Tirukkarrai-pichohan.

cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines damaged. Records a gift of 96 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp before the god by a resident of Ambar-nādu.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Built in the end and damaged. Seems to record a gift of money to the temple by a merchant of Ambar in Ambar-nādu (for sounding the gong).

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. Seems to record the receipt of 16 kalanju of gold from Tiruvāyirari, a maid servant of the queen in return for a certain temple land pledged to her by the temple authorities.

cells.location: Tiruvēḷaikkuḍi
cells.place: On the wall of the shrine in the Mangalēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Damage at the end. Registers a sale of land to the revenue officers (puravuvari-tinai-kalam) by the assembly of Vidālvidungu-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadeya in Vadakarai Nallār-nādu.
